{{technical|date=August 2026}}
{{Short description|Method in contact geometry}}
In [[contact geometry]], a field in [[mathematics]], the '''Boothby-Wang''' '''construction''' (or '''Boothby-Wang''' '''theorem''') characterises a special class of [[contact manifold]]s <math>(P,\alpha)</math> as principal <math>S^1</math>-bundles over [[symplectic manifold]]s <math>(M,\omega)</math> where <math>\omega</math> defines an ''integral'' cohomology class. The proof employs the theory of [[Connection form|connection]] and [[Curvature form|curvature]] forms.

The name '''Boothby-Wang construction''' is used sometimes only for the construction of the contact manifold starting from the symplectic form (as part of [[Contact geometry#Contactification|contactisation]] procedures), sometimes for the entire statement (i.e. also the converse construction of the symplectic manifold starting from the contact form). The resulting [[fibration]] <math>(P,\alpha) \to (M,\omega)</math> is sometimes also called '''Boothby-Wang''' '''Fibration'''.'''<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Geiges |first=Hansjörg |author-link=:de:Hansjörg Geiges |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/an-introduction-to-contact-topology/F851B2A2E7E78C6B9967A18A6641B40C |title=An Introduction to Contact Topology |date=2008 |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |isbn=978-0-521-86585-2 |series=Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics |location=Cambridge |doi=10.1017/CBO9780511611438}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=Boyer |first=Charles |author-link=Charles P. Boyer |url=https://academic.oup.com/book/9253 |title=Sasakian Geometry |last2=Galicki |first2=Krzysztof |author-link2=:pl:Krzysztof Galicki |date=2007-10-01 |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |isbn=978-0-19-856495-9 |doi=10.1093/acprof:oso/9780198564959.001.0001}}</ref>'''

This result was proved in 1959 by [[William M. Boothby|Boothby]] and [[Hsien Chung Wang|Wang]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Boothby |first=W. M. |author-link=William M. Boothby |last2=Wang |first2=H. C. |author-link2=Hsien Chung Wang |date=1958 |title=On Contact Manifolds |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1970165?origin=crossref |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=68 |issue=3 |pages=721 |doi=10.2307/1970165|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and has been subject to several generalisations.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Konderak |first=Jerzy J. |last2=Terlizzi |first2=Luigia Di |last3=Wolak |first3=Robert |date=2007-12-01 |title=A Generalization of the Boothby-wang Theorem |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/tsukuba-journal-of-mathematics/volume-31/issue-2/A-Generalization-of-the-Boothby-wang-Theorem/10.21099/tkbjm/1496165145.full |journal=Tsukuba Journal of Mathematics |volume=31 |issue=2 |doi=10.21099/tkbjm/1496165145 |issn=0387-4982|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kegel |first=Marc |last2=Lange |first2=Christian |date=2021 |title=A Boothby–Wang Theorem for Besse Contact Manifolds |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s40598-020-00165-5 |journal=[[Arnold Mathematical Journal]] |language=en |volume=7 |issue=2 |pages=225–241 |doi=10.1007/s40598-020-00165-5 |issn=2199-6792|arxiv=2003.10155 }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Grabowska |first=Katarzyna |last2=Grabowski |first2=Janusz |date=2026 |title=The regularity and products in contact geometry |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s10231-025-01631-7 |journal=[[Annali di Matematica Pura ed Applicata]] |language=en |volume=205 |issue=2 |pages=993–1015 |doi=10.1007/s10231-025-01631-7 |issn=0373-3114|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Preliminaries ==

=== Regular contact manifolds ===
Consider any contact manifold <math>(P,\alpha)</math>; since its [[Reeb vector field]] <math>R_\alpha \in \mathfrak{X}(P)</math> is nowhere zero, the orbits of the [[Vector flow|flow]] of <math>R_\alpha</math> (also called the Reeb orbits) define a [[regular foliation]] <math>\mathcal{F}_{R_\alpha}</math> of rank 1. The contact form <math>\alpha \in \Omega^1 (P)</math> is called '''regular''' if such foliation <math>\mathcal{F}_{R_\alpha}</math> is simple, i.e. if the leaf space <math>P/\mathcal{F}_{R_\alpha}</math> is a [[smooth manifold]] such that the projection <math>P \to P/\mathcal{F}_{R_\alpha}</math> is a surjective [[Submersion (mathematics)|submersion]].

Assuming that <math>P</math> is [[Connected space|connected]] and <math>R_\alpha</math> is [[Complete vector field|complete]], this regularity condition implies that <math>P \to P/\mathcal{F}_{R_\alpha}</math> is either a principal <math>\mathbb{R}</math>-bundle or a principal <math>S^1</math>-bundle (since the Reeb orbits are either not periodic, or [[Periodic function|periodic]] with the same minimal period).

In the case when <math>P</math> is furthermore [[Compact space|compact]] (which automatically implies that <math>R_\alpha</math> is complete), since the fibres of <math>P \to P/\mathcal{F}_{R_\alpha}</math> are [[closed set]]s of <math>P</math>, they must be compact as well, hence they must be [[circle]]s; this means that the Reeb orbits are periodic with the same minimal period and <math>P \to P/\mathcal{F}_{R_\alpha}</math> is a principal <math>S^1</math>-bundle.

For these reasons, in the complete setting, other authors define a '''regular''' (or '''Boothby-Wang)''' contact form <math>\alpha \in \Omega^1 (P)</math> with a stronger condition: all Reeb orbits are required to be circles with the same minimal periods. This last condition is equivalent to saying that the Reeb vector field <math>R_\alpha \in \mathfrak{X}(P)</math> generates a free <math>S^1</math>-action.'''<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />'''

=== Integral symplectic manifolds ===
A [[Closed and exact differential forms|closed]] [[Differential form|differential 2-form]] <math>\omega \in \Omega^2 (M)</math> is called '''integral''' if its induced [[de Rham cohomology class]] <math>[\omega] \in H^2_{dR} (M)</math> lies in the image of <math>H^2 (M, \mathbb{Z}) \to H^2 (M,\mathbb{R}) \cong H^2_{dR} (M)</math>. Equivalently, its period group

<math>\mathrm{Per}(\omega):= \left\{ \int_\gamma \omega \ | \ \gamma: S^2 \to M \text{ homology 2-cycle } \right\} \subset \mathbb{R}</math> 

is of the kind <math>k\mathbb{Z}</math> for some integer <math>k \in \mathbb{Z}</math>. Notice that, depending on the normalisation conventions, one might have to add a multiplicative factor <math>\frac{1}{2\pi}</math>.

=== Principal bundles and connections ===
A crucial step in the proof relies on the following fact: given any principal <math>G</math>-bundle <math>\pi: P \to M</math>, there is a 1-1 correspondence between <math>k</math>-forms on <math>M</math> and <math>k</math>-forms on <math>P</math> which are '''basic''', i.e. <math>G</math>-invariant and <math>\pi</math>-horizontal (vanishing on any <math>\pi</math>-[[vertical vector field]]). In particular, given <math>\beta \in \Omega^k (P)</math>, there is a unique <math>\omega \in \Omega^k (M)</math> such that <math>\beta = \pi^*\omega</math>.

In general, a [[connection form]] on <math>\pi: P \to M</math> is a form <math>\alpha \in \Omega^1 (P,\mathfrak{g})</math> with values in the Lie algebra <math>\mathfrak{g} := \mathrm{Lie} (G)</math> satisfying the <math>G</math>-[[equivariance]]

<math>(R_g)^*\alpha = g^{-1} \cdot \alpha \quad \forall g \in G</math>

and the condition

<math>\alpha (x^\dagger) = x \quad \forall x \in \mathfrak{g}</math>

where <math>x^\dagger \in \mathfrak{X}(P)</math> denotes the [[fundamental vector field]] associated to <math>x \in \mathfrak{g}</math>, i.e. the image by the infinitesimal action <math>\mathfrak{g} \to \mathfrak{X}(P)</math>.

In the case of the [[abelian Lie group]] <math>G = S^1</math>, we have the [[abelian Lie algebra]] <math>\mathfrak{g} = (\mathbb{R},+)</math>, so that the [[adjoint representation]] <math>g^{-1} \cdot</math> is trivial and the <math>G</math>-equivariance boils down to the <math>G</math>-invariance <math>(R_g)^*\alpha = \alpha</math> for every <math>g \in G</math>; in this case, this is equivalent to <math>\mathcal{L}_{x^\dagger} (\alpha) = 0</math> for every <math>x \in \mathbb{R}</math>.

== From regular contact manifolds to integral symplectic manifolds ==
Let <math>(P,\alpha)</math> be a compact regular [[contact manifold]]. Then <math>\pi: P \to M:= P/S^1</math> is a [[Principal bundle|principal <math>S^1</math>-bundle]] and there is a unique integral [[Symplectic 2-form|symplectic form]] <math>\omega \in \Omega^2 (M)</math> such that <math>d\alpha = \pi^*\omega</math>.'''<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />''' If one adopts the stronger condition of regularity, i.e. requires that the Reeb vector field generates a free <math>S^1</math>-action, the compactness hypothesis is not needed.<ref name=":2" />

This follows from the more complete statement below (using the extra fact that, since <math>S^1</math> is compact, any <math>S^1</math>-action is automatically proper; then <math>M:= P/S^1</math> is a smooth manifold and <math>\pi</math> is a principal <math>S^1</math>-bundle).

Let <math>\pi: P \to M</math> be a principal <math>S^1</math>-bundle over a <math>2n</math>-dimensional manifold <math>M</math>, and let <math>\alpha \in \Omega^1 (P,\mathbb{R}) = \Omega^1 (P)</math> be a [[connection form]] (where the coefficient space <math>\mathbb{R}</math> is identified with the [[Lie algebra]] of the [[abelian Lie group]] <math>S^1</math>). Then

* there is a unique closed differential 2-form <math>\omega \in \Omega^2 (M)</math> such that <math>d\alpha = \pi^*\omega</math>;
* the class <math>[\omega] \in H^2_{dR} (M)</math> is the image of the first Chern class <math>c_1 (P) \in H^2 (M,\mathbb{Z})</math> via <math>H^2 (M, \mathbb{Z}) \to H^2 (M,\mathbb{R}) \cong H^2_{dR} (M)</math>;
* <math>\omega</math> is [[Nondegenerate form|nondegenerate]] (i.e. it is a symplectic form) if and only if <math>\alpha</math> is a [[contact form]].

Moreover, if this happens,

* the [[fundamental vector field]] associated to <math>1 \in \mathbb{R} \cong \mathrm{Lie}(S^1)</math> is the Reeb vector field of <math>\alpha</math>;
* the Reeb orbits are circles and the contact form is regular.

=== Proof ===
One checks first that <math>d\alpha \in \Omega^2 (P)</math> is basic. Indeed, it is <math>S^1</math>-equivariant since <math>\alpha</math> is so; moreover, it is horizontal since <math>\pi</math>-vertical vector field are fundamental vector field of the kind <math>x^\dagger \in \mathfrak{X}(P)</math>, for <math>x \in \mathbb{R} = \mathrm{Lie}(S^1)</math>, hence, by the properties of a connection form,

<math>d\alpha (x^\dagger, \cdot) = \iota_{x^\dagger} (d\alpha) = \cancel{\mathcal{L}_{x^\dagger} \alpha} - d (\iota_{x^\dagger} \alpha) = - d (\alpha (x^\dagger) ) = d (x) = 0.</math>

Then, by the lemma mentioned above, there is a unique <math>\omega \in \Omega^2 (M)</math> such that <math>d\alpha = \pi^*\omega</math>; since [[exterior derivative]] and [[Pullback (differential geometry)|pullbacks]] commute, <math>\omega</math> is automatically closed.

Using [[Chern-Weil theory]], the image via <math>H^2 (M, \mathbb{Z}) \to H^2 (M,\mathbb{R}) \cong H^2_{dR} (M)</math> of the first Chern class of <math>P</math> can be computed precisely by choosing a connection <math>\alpha \in \Omega^1 (P)</math> and considering the induced <math>\omega \in \Omega^2 (M)</math>, so that <math>c_1 (P) = [\omega]</math>.

Furthermore, <math>\alpha \wedge (d\alpha)^n = \alpha \wedge \pi^* (\omega^n) \neq 0</math> (i.e. <math>\alpha</math> is a contact form) if and only if <math>\omega^n \neq 0</math> (i.e. <math>\omega</math> is nondegenerate).

Last, consider the fundamental vector field <math>R:= a(1) = 1^\dagger \in \mathfrak{X}(P)</math>, where <math>a: \mathrm{Lie}(S^1) \cong \mathbb{R} \to \mathfrak{X}(P) </math> is the infinitesimal action. To prove that it coincides with the Reeb vector field <math>R_\alpha \in \mathfrak{X}(P)</math>, one checks that it satisfies <math>\alpha(R) = 1</math> and <math>\iota_R (d\alpha) = 0</math>. But the first condition follows from <math>\alpha (x^\dagger) = x</math> for <math>x = 1</math>, while the second condition follows from the fact that fundamental vector fields are <math>\pi</math>-vertical, hence

<math>\iota_R (d\alpha) = (\pi^*\omega) (R, \cdot) = \omega (\cancel{d\pi(R)},d\pi(\cdot)) = 0</math>.

The Reeb orbits coincide therefore with the fibres of <math>\pi: P \to M</math>, i.e. they are circles, and the contact form is regular.

== From integral symplectic manifolds to regular contact manifolds ==
Let <math>(M,\omega)</math> be an integral [[symplectic manifold]]. Then there is a [[Principal bundle|principal <math>S^1</math>-bundle]] <math>\pi: P \to M</math> and a regular [[contact form]] <math>\alpha \in \Omega^1 (P)</math> such that <math>d\alpha = \pi^*\omega</math>.'''<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />'''

This follows from the more complete statement below.

Let <math>M</math> be a <math>2n</math>-dimensional manifold and <math>\omega \in \Omega^2 (M)</math> a [[Closed and exact differential forms|closed]] [[Differential form|differential 2-form]] which is integral. Then

* there is a principal <math>S^1</math>-bundle <math>\pi: P \to M</math> with [[first Chern class]] <math>[\omega] \in H^2 (M,\mathbb{Z})</math>;
* there is a [[connection form]] <math>\alpha \in \Omega^1 (P,\mathbb{R}) = \Omega^1 (P)</math> such that <math>d\alpha = \pi^*\omega</math>;
* <math>\omega</math> is [[Nondegenerate form|nondegenerate]] (i.e. it is a symplectic form) if and only if <math>\alpha</math> is a [[contact form]]. 
Moreover, if this happens,

* the [[fundamental vector field]] associated to <math>1 \in \mathbb{R} \cong \mathrm{Lie}(S^1)</math> is the Reeb vector field of <math>\alpha</math>;
* the Reeb orbits are circles and the contact form is regular.

=== Proof ===
The existence of a principal <math>S^1</math>-bundle <math>\pi: P \to M</math> with first Chern class <math>[\omega] \in H^2 (M)</math> follows from the general classification of principal <math>S^1</math>-bundles via <math>H^2(M,\mathbb{Z})</math>.

Picking any connection form <math>\alpha_0 \in \Omega^1 (P,\mathbb{R}) = \Omega^1 (P)</math>, the differential <math>d\alpha_0 \in \Omega^2 (P)</math> is basic by the same arguments as in the previous proof. Then, by the lemma mentioned above there is an induced closed 2-form <math>\omega_0 \in \Omega^2 (M)</math> such that <math>d\alpha_0 = \pi^*\omega_0</math>. By definition of Chern class, one has <math>[\omega] = [\omega_0]</math>, i.e. <math>\omega - \omega_0 = d\beta</math> for some <math>\beta \in \Omega^1(M)</math>. Then <math>\alpha := \alpha_0 + \pi^*\beta \in \Omega^1 (P)</math> is by construction a connection form satisfying <math>d\alpha = \pi^*\omega</math>.

Last, again with the same arguments as in the previous proof, <math>\alpha</math> is a contact form if and only if <math>\omega</math> is nondegenerate, and the further two points hold.

== Relation to geometric quantisation ==
A '''prequantum''' '''(or prequantisation) line bundle''' over a symplectic manifold <math>(M,\omega)</math> is a [[Complex vector bundle|complex]] [[line bundle]] <math>L \to M</math> together with a fibrewise [[Hermitian metric]] <math>h</math> and a [[Hermitian connection]] <math>\nabla</math> such that its curvature <math>F_\nabla</math> satisfies <math>F_\nabla = \pm i \omega</math> (the sign depends on the conventions). The existence of this object constitutes the first step (before choosing a polarisation) to perform [[Geometric quantization|geometric quantisation]], and it is obstructed by the integrability condition of <math>(M,\omega)</math>.

The principal bundle <math>(P,\alpha) \to (M,\omega)</math> from the Boothby-Wang construction is equivalent to the data of a prequantisation line bundle. Indeed, given <math>P \to M</math> one defines <math>L \to M</math> as the vector bundle <math>L:= (P \times \mathbb{C})/S^1</math> associated to the natural [[Representation theory|representation]] <math>\mathbb{C} \in \mathrm{Rep} (S^1)</math>. Conversely, given <math>(L,h) \to M</math>, one defines <math>P \to M</math> as the principal bundle of [[Unitary frame bundle|unitary frames]] <math>\mathrm{Fr}(L,h) \subset \mathrm{Fr}(L)</math>, with structure group the [[unitary group]] <math>U(1) \cong S^1</math>. The rest of the equivalence follows from the standard equivalence between vector bundle connections and principal connections, and the fact that the [[Curvature form|curvature of a connection form]] <math>\alpha \in \Omega^1 (P, \mathbb{R}) = \Omega^1 (P)</math> is given by the Maurer-Cartan expression <math>d\alpha + \frac{1}{2} \cancel{[\alpha,\alpha]} = d\alpha \in \Omega^2 (P)</math> (since the Lie algebra <math>\mathrm{Lie} (S^1) = \mathbb{R}</math> is abelian).

The Boothby-Wang construction yield therefore an equivalence between regular contact manifolds and prequantisation bundles (over a given integral symplectic manifold).

== Example ==
Consider the [[Free action|free]] and [[Proper action|proper]] [[Lie group action|action]] of the Lie group <math>S^1 \subset \mathbb{C}</math> on the [[N-sphere|sphere]] <math>S^{2n+1} \subset \mathbb{C}^{n+1}</math> by multiplication on each complex coordinate; its quotient can be identified with the [[complex projective space]] <math>\mathbb{CP}^n</math>. Then the resulting principal <math>S^1</math>-bundle <math>(S^{2n+1},\alpha_{\mathrm{std}}) \to (\mathbb{CP}^n,\omega_{\mathrm{FS}})</math> is a Boothby-Wang fibration, where <math>S^{2n+1}</math> is endowed with the [[Contact geometry#The standard contact structure on the sphere|standard contact form]] <math>\alpha_{\mathrm{std}}</math>, which is automatically regular, and <math>\mathbb{CP}^n</math> is endowed with the Fubini-Study symplectic form <math>\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}</math>, which is automatically integral.

In the case <math>n=1</math> one recovers the classical [[Hopf fibration|Hopf]] [[Hopf fibration|fibration]] <math>S^3\to\mathbb{CP}^1 \cong S^2</math>.
